title: actions runs show maps IDs inconsistently; jobs, check-runs and rerun-failed-jobs endpoints 404
body:
## Environment

- `tea` 0.16.0 (golang 1.26.6, go-sdk v1.2.0)
- Server Forgejo `15.0.5+gitea-1.22.0` (self-hosted)

## Gap 1 — run ID mapping

`tea actions runs list` shows a run as `ID 264` (status failure),
but `tea actions runs show 264` returns `URL:
.../actions/runs/218` — the web UI id. One run, two ids, no documented
mapping. Reproducible without tea: `GET
/api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs` returns `id: 264` while
`html_url` for that same object points to `actions/runs/218`.

## Gap 2 — missing job-level endpoints (server-side, tea degrades badly)

Against this server version all of these 404 with `404 page not found`,
both via tea and via direct `curl` with a valid token:

- `GET .../actions/runs/{id}/jobs` (tried both 264 and 218)
- `GET .../commits/{sha}/check-runs`
- `POST .../actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs`

So `tea actions runs show` always ends in
`failed to get jobs: unknown API error: 404`, and there is no way to
re-run failed jobs from tea at all.

## Working alternative (for other automation authors)

`GET .../commits/{sha}/statuses` works fine and carries per-job
`context`/`status`/`description`/`target_url` — that is how I diagnosed
which gate failed. Suggest documenting it as the fallback, and having
`runs show` degrade to statuses when `/jobs` 404s instead of erroring out.

## Relation

Independent from #1149 (env-provided one-shot auth). Cross-linking only
because both bite the same agentic-CI use case.

title: Support one-shot authenticated calls without persisting a login (env-provided token)
body:
# Support one-shot authenticated calls without persisting a login (env-provided token)

## Use case

Agentic CI workflows that mint short-lived, narrowly-scoped tokens per
session/task (self-hosted Forgejo 15, `tea` 0.16.0). The agent obtains a
credential with exactly the scope a track needs, uses it, and it expires —
the human authorizes once, the agent never persists anything to disk.

## Gap

Today every operating command (`tea api`, `tea pulls`, …) authenticates
exclusively via stored logins. `$GITEA_SERVER_TOKEN` only feeds
`logins add --token`, which persists the login to config — so a token cannot
be *used* without writing it to disk first. There is no global `--token`
flag and no other command honors the env var (checked `tea api -h` and the
top-level help on 0.16.0).

Consequence: a per-session ephemeral token must either be persisted
(`logins add` + `logins delete`, which still leaves the DB token live until
a password-authenticated DELETE) or the workflow falls back to rotating a
standing login — both weaker than true env-only operation.

## Request

Honor an env-provided (or global `--token`) credential for single
invocations without creating/persisting a login entry, e.g. read order:
explicit flag > env var > stored login. Failing that, document that
diskless operation is unsupported so automation authors stop trying.

Out of scope here: token TTL (server-side matter, tracked separately —
upstream tokens carry no expiry field at all).
